draft.title: Coasts shaping the land
card: Waves shape a coast in two ways. They erode, wearing rock away, and they deposit, dropping sand and other sediment.
Headland
a point of harder rock that sticks out into the sea. Waves attack it and wear it into cliffs. They can then cut a cave in the cliff.
Arch and stack
if waves cut a cave right through a headland, it becomes an arch. When the top of the arch falls, a tall column of rock called a stack is left standing in the sea.
Beach and spit
waves also carry sand along the shore. Sand dropped in a sheltered place builds a beach. Sand dropped in a long strip that juts out into the water is called a spit.
draft.remember: Waves wear rock away to make cliffs, caves, arches and stacks, and drop sand to make beaches and spits.

a.q: Waves cut a cave through a headland until it forms an opening. The rock above the opening still stands. What landform is this?
a.why: A cave cut right through a headland leaves an opening with rock still above it, which is an arch. A stack is tempting, but it forms only after the top of the arch falls.
a.clue: Is the rock still joined across the top?

b.q: On a bay in Jervis Bay, waves carry sand along the shore and drop it in a long strip that juts out into the water. What landform is building?
b.why: Sand carried along the shore and dropped in a long strip that juts out is a spit. A stack is wrong, because stacks are made by erosion of rock, not by sand being dropped.
b.clue: Which landform is built by dropped sand?

wants.brief: A series of four small drawings of a headland: cliff with a cave, a cave cut through to form an arch, the arch top fallen leaving a stack. Label headland, cliff, cave, arch and stack.
wants.why: It shows how each erosion landform leads to the next.

problems.detail: "On a bay in Jervis Bay" is awkward and confusing, because Jervis Bay is itself a bay. It also implies a real spit is building there, which the card does not support. A simpler wording would be "On a beach in Jervis Bay" or a general setting.

check.summary: The content is accurate and both questions have one clear right answer. The only issue is the confusing phrase "On a bay in Jervis Bay" in question b, which should be reworded.
